design_rationale: GOOD TEST: Marcus's surface goal ('add my usual top-up') never names a dollar figure, a policy id, or anything about his account's status. Between that single ask and the scored write (credited_amount on apply_credit_topup_b1893e39) sits a 2-hop chain the agent must read out of the policy text and the world alone, never out of anything Marcus says: (1) retail_ext_topup_credit.compute has exactly one prerequisite -- a value_input on its own `room` binding (room = maximum_balance_usd - current_balance), pointing at retail_ext_topup_refund; retail_ext_topup_credit's rule itself says nothing about suspension at all, and carries no gate of its own tied to account status -- the dependency on reinstatement is purely TRANSITIVE, routed through the refund. (2) retail_ext_topup_refund is itself state_due (fires automatically once a suspended account is reinstated, regardless of whether anyone asks), but its own rule requires 'A refund of a top-up may be recorded only while the account is active or in the same moment as its confirmed cancellation to closed' -- inherited from base retail_refund_policy's structured eligibility (allowed=[active, closed]) -- and the account's status is 'suspended' at the opening, so the refund itself cannot be recorded until retail_ext_reinstatement (itself state_due, since the account sits suspended regardless of whether Marcus calls at all) resolves that gate. The agent discovers both hops purely by reading retail_ext_topup_credit's rule (which names the room/cap dependency), then retail_ext_topup_refund's rule (which names the active-or-closed status requirement), then the account's own status=suspended row -- never from Marcus, who asks only for the top-up and reacts passively once the representative explains what else the account needs first. BREADTH: the bonus_pct branch (MX of two tier params), the membership good-standing branch (CFIELD on a different category), the cap branch (MN against maximum_balance_usd, which genuinely binds if the refund is skipped), and the reinstatement-fee corp surcharge branch (CPARAM on a THIRD category, corp) are four independent, parallel factors. SCOPE TAKEN: this is the first task instantiated for this difficulty; it claims retail_ext_topup_credit (root), retail_ext_topup_refund and retail_ext_reinstatement -- the whole chain behind an on-request top-up on a suspended account. It leaves retail_ext_auto_reload, retail_ext_redemption_settlement, retail_ext_closure_settlement and the difficulty's one workflow completely untouched for task 1, which never touches redemption, auto-reload or closure. BASE-INVARIANT CARD: retail_fraud_suspension_policy has eligibility=[] (policy_scope only) -- reinstatement has no structured gate to inherit beyond the tier's own reinstatement_fee_usd param, which this task carries via base_fee=P('reinstatement_fee_usd')=0.00 for the Standard Credit $100 Tier. retail_refund_policy's ONE structured eligibility (refund_requires_open_or_just_closed_account, state, allowed=[active,closed]) intersects retail_ext_topup_refund's subject (retail_credit_refund) and is inherited verbatim: at the OPENING world the account's status is 'suspended' (initial_state.retail_credit_accounts.<acct>.status='suspended'), so this gate is FALSE at frozen_time -- exactly why reinstatement is a genuine, unmet-at-opening prerequisite, not a decoration. After reinstate_suspended_credit_account_88623c40 runs (step index 7) the status flips to 'active', satisfying the gate for the refund call at step index 9. retail_tier_topup_pricing has eligibility=[] (policy_scope). BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: the target object is the single store-credit account credit_account_id=77976684-a4a9-4996-8807-fba88f0eddee (retail_agg_multi_holding limits Marcus to exactly one non-closed account); the refund's source is every retail_credit_topup row within the calendar month preceding reinstatement (SUM's own within_months=1 date filter), which in this seed is exactly the single row c888bbe9-0605-4bbd-8626-8ac151cee60a -- the other 8 topup rows (all more than a month before frozen_time) and the 1 redemption row are excluded by that same date filter, not by any ad hoc rule. PROBLEM-TREE CARD: root=retail_ext_topup_credit. Edge1 (retail_ext_topup_credit -> retail_ext_topup_refund, value_input, gate=room): unresolved_at_frozen_time because credit_balance=360.00 still includes the un-refunded $20.00 top-up; skipping the refund leaves the post-fee balance at 310.00 instead of 290.00, so room=MX(400.00-310.00,0)=90.00 instead of MX(400.00-290.00,0)=110.00 -- since face+bonus=102.00 exceeds 90.00 but not 110.00, credited_amount would drop to 90.00 (capped) if the refund were skipped, versus the real 102.00 (uncapped) once it is resolved: a genuinely different terminal value, confirmed by check_compute.py's own value_input replay. Edge2 (retail_ext_topup_refund -> retail_ext_reinstatement, state_gate, gate=retail_credit_accounts.status): unresolved_at_frozen_time because initial_state.retail_credit_accounts.<acct>.status='suspended' (not in the refund eligibility's allowed=[active,closed]); resolved once reinstate_suspended_credit_account_88623c40 flips status to 'active'. Order: reinstatement, then refund, then topup -- a strict chain, no parallel-order ambiguity to resolve. TOPOLOGICAL/GT ORDER: GT calls land in exactly this order (steps 7, 9, 11), matching prerequisite_closure.resolution_order. user_scenario names neither the hold, the reinstatement, the refund, nor any order between them -- Marcus asks only to have his usual top-up added, and cooperates passively ('Oh, I had no idea -- that's fine, go ahead and take care of whatever needs to happen') only once the representative has already explained the hold and the fee, never before. Both retail_ext_reinstatement and retail_ext_topup_refund are classified state_due precisely so that neither prerequisite's discovery or handling time is anchored to a customer utterance: the agent finds them by reading the account's own status and the policy text, not by being told. tools_do_not_block: refund_topup_amount_847aef7e and apply_credit_topup_b1893e39 perform their ctx.create/ctx.update unconditionally on whatever arguments are passed -- neither checks account status, so calling either while suspended would still silently write (see task_tools.py, no status branch in either function body); the correctness of resolving reinstatement first shows up only in the terminal balance/eligibility-evidence match, never in a tool refusal. STANDARD SOLUTION: locate+verify Marcus, read the account and its ledger, read the membership holding (dues_balance=0.00, good standing) and the corp enrollment (Startup Partner, suspended, late_payment_fee_usd=50.00 from corp.yaml), compute reinstatement_fee_amount=0.00+50.00=50.00, call reinstate; recompute refund_amount=SUM(within_months=1 topups)=20.00, pct=100 -> RND(20.00*100/100,2)=20.00, call refund; recompute credited_amount=MN(100.00+RND(100*2/100,2), MX(400.00-(360.00-50.00-20.00),0))=MN(102.00,110.00)=102.00, call topup. VERIFICATION: hand-computed and cross-checked against build_env's own SUM/CPARAM/CFIELD semantics (SUM is holding-scoped and month-windowed; CPARAM looks up the matching cross-category holding's variant parameters in corp.yaml); recomputation performed a second time reading only the rendered-KB-equivalent prose (the rule paragraphs above) plus the ledger and tier table, with no reference to compute/expected, and reached the same three numbers. CLOSURE: charter_scope={retail_ext_topup_credit, retail_ext_topup_refund, retail_ext_reinstatement}=computations policy ids=required_documents; task_tools={reinstate_suspended_credit_account_88623c40, refund_topup_amount_847aef7e, apply_credit_topup_b1893e39} in first-use order, matching GT. REWORK NOTE (round 2): the earlier revision's rationale mistakenly quoted retail_ext_topup_credit.rule as containing 'no further top-up may be credited while suspended' -- that sentence never existed anywhere in the charter; the corrected account above states the true, sole mechanism (a value_input on `room`, transitively routed through retail_ext_topup_refund's own state_gate) and the persona was rewritten to remove the customer's outright naming of the reinstatement prerequisite and its order, replacing it with a root-only ask plus passive, post-explanation cooperation; retail_ext_reinstatement's trigger was reclassified on_request -> state_due (propagated to retail.extended.yaml and to this task's solvability_contract.gold_actions[step=7], whose intent_source now cites initial_state.retail_credit_accounts.<acct>.status instead of a user_scenario quotation) so that neither hidden prerequisite is anchored to anything the customer says.
user_scenario: Marcus Yeboah is a member of Vantage Metro Fitness who keeps a pro-shop store-credit account for his gear purchases. He calls the contact center in a relaxed, everyday tone and opens with something like, 'Hi, this is Marcus Yeboah -- I'd like to add my usual top-up to my store-credit account, please.' That is the entire reason for his call; he has no other request in mind. He wants the representative to just handle it directly on his end -- he isn't planning to come into a club for it and isn't asking for anything to be mailed or emailed to him. If asked how he'd like to verify himself, he gives his phone number and email without hesitation: his number on file is 2125550500, and his email is marcus.yeboah@example.com; if pressed for a third detail he can also give his date of birth, 1989-03-14. He doesn't know his account reference number and has never seen the actual dollar figures the system will land on, so if asked what the top-up amount should come out to or what any fee might be, he says, 'Honestly I have no idea, whatever the standard amount and fees are is fine -- that's what I'm calling you for.' He has no idea his account carries any particular tier name either; if asked, he just says 'whatever tier I signed up with, I haven't changed it.' If the representative mentions that the account was found on a fraud-review hold and that it needs to be lifted before anything else can happen, he reacts with mild surprise but cooperates readily, saying something like 'Oh, I had no idea -- that's fine, go ahead and take care of whatever needs to happen.' If the representative goes on to explain that lifting the hold carries a fee, or that a recent top-up is being reversed as part of getting the account back in order, he doesn't ask for details or push back -- he just says 'Sure, whatever the process requires is fine by me' and waits for the top-up to go through. He never volunteers that anything might be wrong with his account and never suggests an order of operations himself -- he only reacts, calmly and cooperatively, to whatever the representative actually tells him. Once the representative confirms the top-up has been applied, he simply thanks them and says that's everything he needed, and ends the call there.
